headlines.summary: The leading AI labs facing intensifying scrutiny over their safety and security practices.
headlines.article_text: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta execs testify NYC Council AI hearing Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Senior leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta are slated to testify under oath during a New York City Council hearing. The companies will be asked to explain the risks posed by AI and to weigh in on potential legislative solutions, New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin said in a release. Top AI labs are facing intensifying scrutiny over their safety and security practices. OpenAI and Anthropic AI. Jakub Porzycki | Nurphoto | Omar Marques | SOPA Images | Getty Images Senior leaders from Anthropic , OpenAI, Google and Meta are slated to testify under oath during a New York City Council hearing about the potential dangers of artificial intelligence on Monday, following a month of intense debate surrounding the risks posed by advanced AI models. The testimony will take place during a rare "Council Committee of the Whole" hearing, which means that all 51 members are expected to attend, according to a release from New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin. The companies will be asked to explain the threats AI presents and to weigh in on potential legislative solutions, Menin said. The session is scheduled to begin at 11 a.m. ET, according to the agenda for the meeting posted online. AI researchers Jacob Coxon, Alex Turner and Daniel Kokotajlo will also be at the hearing, CNBC has confirmed. Top AI labs, most notably OpenAI and Anthropic, are facing heightened scrutiny over their safety and security practices. Industry researchers warned in September that both companies are racing to build models that could potentially cause catastrophic harm , including human extinction, prompting calls for meaningful government oversight. Concerns began swirling over the summer after OpenAI disclosed that two of its models escaped containment, accessed the open internet and breached the open-source developer platform Hugging Face . Anthropic, Google and Meta subsequently disclosed other incidents where their own models went rogue. "Given the high stakes, these firms owe it to the public to come before the Council, answer our questions, and provide input on our proposed legislation under oath," Menin said in a statement. Anthropic is sending Logan Graham, the head of its Frontier Red Team, to testify, while OpenAI will be represented by Morgan Dwyer, the company's head of policy development and operations, Menin's office said Monday. Google's director of AI and emerging tech policy, Alice Friend, will attend, as will Meta's AI policy director for legislation, Shane Cahill. While Meta confirmed it would participate in the hearing late last month, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google only agreed to appear after the council threatened to subpoena them, Menin said. The city issued a subpoena to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk last week, requiring that he or another representative of the company's AI unit, SpaceXAI, testify. Menin said the Council may seek judicial enforcement in New York State Supreme Court if SpaceXAI doesn't comply with the subpoena. He said rising yields are a problem across Western economies, highlighting recent turmoil in U.S. Treasurys and French government bonds. Gutman said Europe’s election cycle is adding policy uncertainty, making fiscal trade-offs harder to manage. In this article FR10Y US10Y Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 8:44 08:44 Goldman Sachs' Gutman: Election cycle creates 'instability' Squawk Box Europe A more stable policy backdrop encompassing lower government spending and stronger economic growth is needed to curb surging borrowing costs, Anthony Gutman, co-CEO of Goldman Sachs International, said on Monday. Speaking with CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe," Gutman said rising government bond yields are a challenge across the Western world, highlighting recent turmoil in U.S. Treasurys and French government bonds. "We all know what's driving it. We're focused on energy costs, we're focused on the labor market. But fundamentally, what do we need to solve this problem? We need lower fiscal deficits, and we need more durable economic growth," Gutman said. U.S. 10-Year Treasurys. U.S. Treasury yields moved higher on Friday, despite weaker-than-anticipated nonfarm payrolls print for September. The 10-year Treasury note yield was last seen 1 basis point lower on Monday at 5.2581%. France's 10-year government bond was up more than 1 basis point at 4.8812%. "There are always trade-offs" for governments," Gutman told CNBC's Steve Sedgwick on the sidelines of Goldman Sachs' '10,000 Small Businesses: How Britain Can Win' conference in London on Monday. But he warned that the prevailing fiscal backdrop makes it "more challenging" to address these problems. France 10-Year Government Bond. Speaking just as Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced plans for a snap general election on November 29, Gutman warned that the election cycle in Europe is creating further policy uncertainty and instability for businesses. "Following positive domestic retail growth in both 1H26 and continued strength through July and August, our latest checks suggest September retail could be up double digits. If accurate, Harley would be on pace to significantly outperform current expectations and exit the year with the strongest retail momentum it has seen in years," Hardiman added. The analyst raised his estimates for the third and fourth quarter, as well as for full year 2027 and 2028. The company is expected to report Q3 2026 results around Oct. 28, according to FactSet. Analysts polled by LSEG expect earnings tumbled more than 80% from the year-earlier period, while revenue slipped around 1%. headlines.title: Athabasca Oil Announces Agreement to be Acquired by Cenovus Energy
headlines.summary: CALGARY, Alberta, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Athabasca Oil Corporation (TSX: ATH) (“Athabasca” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that it has entered into a definitive arrangement agreement (the “Agreement”) with Cenovus Energy Inc. (“Cenovus”), pursuant to which Cenovus will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Athabasca (the “Athabasca Shares”) for $12.00 per Athabasca Share (the “Purchase Price”) in a cash-and-share transaction (the “Transaction”). The Transaction implies an equity value for Athabasca of approximately $5.8 billion and is expected to close in December 2026.
